blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne sine, cosine aur tangent ke inverse functions dekhe. Ab baari hai un ke reciprocals (ulte) ki: cosecant, secant aur cotangent. Is page par hum cosecant ka inverse banayenge. Tareeqa bilkul wahi hai jo sine ke liye tha: pehle graph dekhenge, phir domain ko chhota (restrict) karenge taa ke function one-one aur onto ho jaye, aur phir us ka inverse define karenge. Agar sine wala sabaq yaad hai to aadha kaam pehle hi ho chuka hai.

Function \(f(x) = \csc x\) ka domain \(\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R} \wedge x \ne n\pi,\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\) hai aur range set \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\) hai. Is ka graph Figure 9.10 mein dikhaya gaya hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh domain aur range kahan se aaye? Yaad kijiye ke \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\). Zero se divide karna mana hai, is liye jahan bhi \(\sin x = 0\) ho, woh \(x\) nikalna padega. Yeh points hain \(x = n\pi\), yani \(0, \pm\pi, \pm 2\pi, \dots\) In points par graph ke vertical asymptotes hain (asymptote: woh line jis ke qareeb graph jata hai magar chhoota nahin), jo Figure 9.10 mein dashed lines hain.
Range ki baat: \(\sin x\) hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan rehta hai. Jab kisi chhote number ka ulta (reciprocal) lein to woh bada ho jata hai, jaise \(\frac{1}{0.5} = 2\). Is liye \(|\csc x| \ge 1\) hamesha. Yani \(\csc x\) kabhi \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke beech ki value nahin leta. \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\) ka yahi matlab hai; intervals mein likhein to \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\).

blocks.alt: Graph of y = csc x for x from minus 2 pi to 2 pi. Dashed vertical asymptotes at x = minus 2 pi, minus pi, 0, pi and 2 pi. Dashed horizontal lines y = 1 and y = minus 1. U-shaped branches open upward with lowest points (minus 3 pi over 2, 1) and (pi over 2, 1); branches open downward with highest points (minus pi over 2, minus 1) and (3 pi over 2, minus 1). No part of the graph lies between y = minus 1 and y = 1.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.10: graph of \(y = \csc x\) from \(-2\pi\) to \(2\pi\) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ab graph ko ghor se dekhiye. Line \(y = 1\) graph ko bahut saare points par chhooti hai, aur line \(y = -1\) bhi. Matlab ek hi output (jaise 1) bahut saare inputs se aa raha hai. Aisa function one-one nahin hota, aur jo one-one na ho woh bijective (one-one aur onto dono) nahin hota, is liye us ka inverse nahin ban sakta.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ek rozmarra misaal se samjhiye. Maan lijiye class mein bahut se bachon ke marks 75 hain. Agar main aap ko sirf '75' bataun aur poochun ke yeh kis bache ke marks hain, to aap ek naam nahin bata sakte, kyun ke jawab bahut saare hain. Inverse function bhi yahi sawal poochta hai: output diya hua hai, input batao. Jawab tabhi ek ho sakta hai jab har output sirf ek input se aaye. Cosecant ka graph baar baar dohraata hai (periodic hai), is liye \(\csc x = 2\) ke liye \(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{13\pi}{6}, \dots\) bahut se angles milte hain. Is uljhan ko khatam karne ke liye hum graph ka sirf ek aisa tukda chunte hain jis mein har value bilkul ek dafa aaye. Isi chune hue tukde ko 'principal' kehte hain, aur us se milne wale jawab ko 'principal value'.

Hal yeh hai ke domain ko interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] - \{0\}\) tak mehdood (restrict) kar dein. Is restricted domain wala function, yani
\[f : \left[-\tfrac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
\[\to (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\]
one-one aur onto ban jata hai, yani invertible hai. Isay principal cosecant function kehte hain. Inverse cosecant function yun define hota hai:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is restricted function ka codomain \((-\infty, 1) \cup (1, \infty)\) likhti hai. Yeh ghalat hai. Is set mein \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan ke saare numbers aa jate hain (jo \(\csc x\) kabhi leta hi nahin), aur \(-1\) aur \(1\) khud bahar reh jate hain (jab ke \(\csc\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\) aur \(\csc\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1\)). Sahi codomain \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) hai, jaisa kitab ki apni summary table (9.1.6) mein bhi likha hai.

blocks.text_alt: y equals inverse cosecant of x if and only if x equals cosecant of y

blocks.text: Is definition ko aise parhiye: '\(\csc^{-1} x\) woh angle \(y\) hai jis ka cosecant \(x\) ho', aur shart yeh ke \(y\) principal range ke andar ho. Yani inverse function sawal ulta poochta hai: value di hui hai, angle batao.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahi tukda kyun chuna? Interval \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) par \(\sin x\) 0 se barh kar 1 tak jata hai, is liye \(\csc x\) \(+\infty\) se ghat kar 1 tak aata hai. Yani 1 ya us se bari har value bilkul ek dafa milti hai. Interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)\) par \(\csc x\) \(-1\) se \(-\infty\) tak jata hai, yani \(-1\) ya us se chhoti har value bhi ek hi dafa. Koi horizontal line is tukde ko do jagah nahin kaatti (one-one), aur har ijazat wali value mil jati hai (onto).
Ghor kijiye: yeh wahi interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) hai jo \(\sin^{-1} x\) ke liye liya tha, bas 0 nikal diya kyun ke \(\sin 0 = 0\) aur wahan cosecant define nahin. Isi chunav ki wajah se aage 9.1.6 ki Example 4 mein \(\csc^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) saabit hota hai.

Ab inverse function ka domain aur range: \(\csc^{-1} x\) ka domain \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\) hai aur range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) hai. Dekhiye kya hua: original (principal) function ka domain inverse ki range ban gaya, aur original ki range inverse ka domain. Har inverse function mein yahi adla badli (swap) hoti hai.

Principal function \(\csc : \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] \to (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) ka graph Figure 9.11(a) mein hai, aur \(\csc^{-1} : (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty) \to \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) ka graph Figure 9.11(b) mein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Is jumle mein kitab do dafa \((-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty)\) likhti hai, gol (round) brackets ke saath. End points \(-1\) aur \(1\) set mein shamil hain, is liye brackets band (closed) hone chahiye: \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\). Ek faltu colon bhi hai: \(\to:\) ki jagah sirf \(\to\) hona chahiye.

blocks.alt: Principal branch of y = csc x: for x in (0, pi over 2] the curve comes down from plus infinity near the y-axis to the end point (pi over 2, 1); for x in [minus pi over 2, 0) it starts at the end point (minus pi over 2, minus 1) and goes down to minus infinity near the y-axis. Dashed vertical lines at x = minus pi over 2 and x = pi over 2.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.11(a): graph of \(y = \csc x\) on \([-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0) \cup (0, \frac{\pi}{2}]\) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab Figure 9.11(a) ke neeche caption 'Graph of \(y = \csc x\) from \(-2\pi\) to \(2\pi\)' likhti hai, jo Figure 9.10 se copy hua lagta hai. Asal mein Figure 9.11(a) sirf principal tukda dikhati hai, yani \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) par. Humari caption yahi batati hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = inverse cosecant of x. For x at least 1 the curve starts at (1, pi over 2) and decreases towards the x-axis without touching it. For x at most minus 1 the curve starts at (minus 1, minus pi over 2) and rises towards the x-axis without touching it. Dashed horizontal lines y = pi over 2 and y = minus pi over 2. Nothing is drawn for x between minus 1 and 1.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.11(b): graph of \(y = \csc^{-1} x\) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono graphs ko saath rakh kar dekhiye. \(\csc^{-1} x\) ka graph principal \(\csc x\) ke graph ka line \(y = x\) mein aaina-aks (mirror image) hai. Har point \((a, b)\) ulat kar \((b, a)\) ban jata hai: \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, 1\right)\) se \(\left(1, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), aur \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, -1\right)\) se \(\left(-1, -\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
\(\csc x\) ka vertical asymptote \(x = 0\) palat kar \(\csc^{-1} x\) ka horizontal asymptote \(y = 0\) (yani \(x\)-axis) ban jata hai. Matlab jaise jaise \(x\) bara hota hai, \(\csc^{-1} x\) zero ke qareeb aata jata hai magar kabhi zero nahin banta. Isi liye 0 range mein shamil nahin.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Maan lijiye \(\csc^{-1} 2\) chahiye. Sawal yeh hai: kaun sa angle \(y\) (principal range mein) hai jis ka \(\csc y = 2\), yani \(\sin y = \frac{1}{2}\)? Jawab \(y = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
Ab \(\csc^{-1}(-\sqrt{2})\): \(\sin y = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), to \(y = -\frac{\pi}{4}\). Yahan \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\) bhi sine \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) deta hai, magar woh range se bahar hai, is liye nahin chalega.
Aur \(\csc^{-1}\frac{1}{2}\)? Yeh maujood hi nahin, kyun ke \(\frac{1}{2}\) domain \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\) mein nahin aata.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Khud se poochiye: kya \(\csc^{-1} x\) kabhi 0 ho sakta hai? Agar \(\csc^{-1} x = 0\) ho to \(x = \csc 0\) hona chahiye, jo define hi nahin. Is liye nahin. Aur kya \(\csc^{-1}(0.8)\) mil sakta hai? Nahin, kyun ke \(0.8\) domain mein nahin.
Ek aur sawal: \(\csc^{-1} x\) ka sab se bara mumkin jawab kya hai? Range dekhiye: \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), jo \(x = 1\) par milta hai. Aur sab se chhota \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\), jo \(x = -1\) par. Baqi saare jawab in dono ke darmiyan hain, aur zero ke qareeb tab aate hain jab \(x\) bahut bara (ya bahut chhota negative) ho.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Exam mein aksar seedha poocha jata hai: '\(\csc^{-1} x\) ka domain aur range likhiye' ya 'principal cosecant function define kijiye'. Jawab mein teen cheezein zaroor likhiye: restricted domain, codomain (closed brackets ke saath), aur definition \(y = \csc^{-1} x \iff x = \csc y\). Kitab ki ghalat brackets copy mat kijiye; examiner sahi brackets dekhta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\); domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{n\pi\}\), range \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\). Periodic hone ki wajah se one-one nahin.
2. Principal cosecant function: domain \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), codomain \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\).
3. \(y = \csc^{-1} x \iff x = \csc y\).
4. \(\csc^{-1} x\) ka domain \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\), range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).
5. Dono graphs line \(y = x\) mein mirror images hain; \(y = 0\) \(\csc^{-1} x\) ka horizontal asymptote hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\csc^{-1} x\) ko \(\frac{1}{\csc x}\) samajh lena. Yahan \(-1\) ka matlab inverse function hai, reciprocal nahin. (\(\frac{1}{\csc x}\) to sirf \(\sin x\) hai.)
2. Range mein 0 shamil kar dena. \(y = 0\) par \(\csc y\) define nahin, is liye \(\csc^{-1} x\) kabhi 0 nahin hota.
3. Range se bahar ka jawab dena, jaise \(\csc^{-1} 2 = \frac{5\pi}{6}\). Yeh sach hai ke \(\csc\frac{5\pi}{6} = 2\), magar principal value \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) hai.
4. \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke beech ke kisi number ka \(\csc^{-1}\) nikalne ki koshish karna: woh maujood hi nahin.
